abstract: Audits specialized wet-organic artifact conservation staffing and chemical treatment certifications
system_message:
You are Conservator in chief (CIC). The Conservator in chief (CIC) audits specialized wet-organic artifact conservation staffing and chemical treatment certifications across candidate conservation repositories.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Polymer impregnation batch capacity（POLY）
information_points.content:
CIC-POLY-WFU：Solent Marine Archaeological Annex possesses a polyethylene glycol treatment tank volume of 1,200 L for liquid holding in its active wood preservation batches.
CIC-POLY-2CN：Severn Estuary Conservation Redoubt features a polyethylene glycol treatment tank volume of 1,800 L within its chemical bath preservation facilities.
CIC-POLY-UD4：Clyde Subterranean Heritage Vault reports a polyethylene glycol treatment tank volume of 1,500 L across its active wood stabilization immersion tanks.

information_points.title: Audits specialized wet-organic artifact conservation staffing and chemical treatment certifications（CURA）
information_points.content:
CIC-CURA-OAW：For Clyde Subterranean Heritage Vault, wet-organic preservation staffing accredited is true, verified by attestation of accredited conservator coverage for 24-hour artifact reception across the dedicated waterlogged wood and leather artifact team.
CIC-CURA-H7D：Solent Marine Archaeological Annex maintains accredited wet-organic preservation staffing as true, supported by personnel attestation of round-the-clock accredited conservator coverage for waterlogged wood and leather conservation.
CIC-CURA-55G：At Severn Estuary Conservation Redoubt, wet-organic preservation staffing accredited is false, reflecting a lack of accredited conservator coverage for 24-hour artifact reception on the waterlogged artifact team.
